learning_outcomes.text: Students can phenomenologically describe the structure of fixed-wing aircraft and the basics of their aerodynamics.
Students can calculate the flow processes on airfoils and the forces that occur.
Students can describe the basics of aerospace measurement technology and electronic flight control, as well as the structure and function of aerospace actuators and sensors.
Students can partially calculate or systemically analyze the aerospace actuators and sensors.
Students can assess the applicability of the named topics in automatic flight control.

syllabus_topics: Stall and measures to improve stall characteristics
Functional principles and basic structure of cockpit systems
Aircraft sensors (aerodynamic, inertial, laser, radar and satellite-based)

assessment_methods.method: Graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) for MECB411C
Graded written exam (60 min) or graded oral exam (20 min) or graded presentation (20 min) for MECB412C

assessment_rules: The examination performance is taken in two individual examinations. The weighting is equal for both events according to ECTS. Participation and cooperation in the exercises as well as successful completion of the tasks are prerequisites for admission to the examination for MECB412C; the exact prerequisites for admission to the examination will be determined at the beginning of the semester. The module grade for MECB410C results from the grades of MECB411C and MECB412C with equal weighting.
